Definition: the sky (as aloft; the dual perhaps alluding to the visible arch in which the clouds move, as well as to the higher ether where the celestial bodies revolve)
BiblicalUsage: The heavens are God's first witness, made on the first day and still speaking. In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth, and called the firmament heaven, and set lights in it for signs and for seasons. Moses says the heaven and the heaven of heavens is the LORD's, Solomon confesses that the heaven of heavens cannot contain Him, and the psalm says the heavens declare the glory of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the heavens declare what words cannot, because they show a God too great to be contained and too near to be missed. The heaven of heavens cannot hold Him, yet He made a place for His name among men. That is why I look up when I pray, because the sky is His first sermon.
